abstract: Máčajová, Mazzuoccolo and Tabarelli showed that if a minimum counterexample to the Berge–Fulkerson conjecture is cyclically 5-edge-connected but not cyclically 6-edge-connected, then the admissible sets of Berge–Fulkerson boundary types of the two 5-poles at any cycle-separating 5-edge-cut form one of 13 explicit pairs, Cases I–XIII. We prove that nine of these cases are impossible: no cubic 5-pole of any order has admissible set equal to the set $L^*$ of Cases I, II, III, V, VI, VII, VIII or X, or to the set $R^*$ of Case XIII. Consequently every cycle-separating 5-edge-cut of such a minimum counterexample is of Case IV, IX, XI or XII; one side is a 5-cycle and, by the computation of Brinkmann, Goedgebeur, Hägglund and Markström, the other side has at least 33 vertices. The method records, for a Berge–Fulkerson colouring, the pairing of the dangling edges by the Kempe paths of every colour pair. A Kempe switch preserves the pairing of the switched pair and of all disjoint pairs, which gives a finite transition system on labelled boundary states whose greatest fixed point must contain a state of every admissible type. Cases III, VI and XIII are excluded by short hand arguments; for the other six cases the fixed point, computed by a standard-library program and confirmed by a second independent implementation, has an empty fibre. For Cases IV, IX, XI and XII all fibres survive, so these cases are not decided by route coherence.
author: lihongmin
change_summary: - Supplement README.md (and CONTENTS.sha256): qualified the description of independent_fixpoint.py to state that its counts times the orbit sizes 720/360/90 reproduce every row of Table 1 in its collection (all rows of Table 1 except L* of Case XIII), matching Section 5 of the manuscript.
title: Route-coherent Kempe closure and cycle-separating 5-cuts in a minimum counterexample to the Berge–Fulkerson conjecture
